quote.translation: There are, of course, many cases in which what was at first thought to be a contingency of sound is resolved into necessity .

regions.text: 性に解體される場合はもちろん屢々ある。例へば神、上髪はすべて頭の方に位する嫌ぶべきものである。狐も恐ろしい「かみ」である。

quote.translation: Kami as "god" (神), "above" (上) and "hair" (髮), for example, are all venerable things situated towards the head, and the wolf, ōkami, is also a fearsome kami.

regions.text: それらはみな夫通の理由に制約された諸々の蹄結である。相互間には理由性に基く論理必然的闘係が存してるる。

quote.translation: These are all consequents conditioned by a common ground, and among them there is a logical and necessary relation based on groundedness.

regions.text: 理由約積極的偶然性が斯やうなものに見られないのは云ふまでもない。

quote.translation: It goes without saying that positive contingency of ground is not to be found in cases of this kind.

quote.translation: Leibniz's so-called law of sufficient reason contains both the "ground of knowledge" and the "ground of reality", and in this sense it also carries the meaning of the law of causality.

quote.translation: This is clear from the words of his fifth letter to Clarke: "This principle is the principle that requires a sufficient reason in order that a thing exist, an event occur, a truth arise" (Leibniz, Opera philosophica, ed. Erdmann, p. 778).
